title: Deleting auxiliary boundary from a tame Kummer cover
statement:
Let $Y$ be a Noetherian regular scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme], [pqf-def-locnoeth] with a normal crossings divisor $\overline D$, and let $q:V\to Y$ be a finite normal generically free $G$-quotient for a finite group $G$. The quotient has invariant structure sheaf and geometric fibres the orbits. Suppose that, with the inverse-image divisorial log structures, $(V,q^{-1}\overline D)\to(Y,\overline D)$ is a Kummer etale $G$-cover, and is tame. Kummer etale means etale locally a strict base change of an injective fs monoid chart map with every target element having a positive multiple in the image and with finite group-completion cokernel of order invertible locally. Let $D\subseteq\overline D$ be a reduced union of irreducible components, and suppose $q$ is etale over $Y\setminus D$. Then $(V,q^{-1}D)\to(Y,D)$, with reduced boundaries and divisorial log structures, is a Kummer etale $G$-cover; $(V,q^{-1}D)$ is fs log regular and the action on it is very tame. In particular the auxiliary components in $\overline D\setminus D$ can be deleted. Very tame means invertible inertia order and trivial inertia action on characteristic monoids and on strict local log strata [def-trf-fs-log-blowup].

More generally Kummer etale G-covers are stable under arbitrary base change in fs log schemes. A Kummer etale cover of a locally Noetherian fs log regular scheme is fs log regular, its inertia action is very tame, and its restriction over an open on which the base has trivial log structure is an ordinary finite etale G-cover. In a birational saturated log blowup base change, the pulled-back cover is the normalization of the modified base in the original generic cover. For such a Kummer etale $G$-cover, the underlying finite scheme morphism is etale on the locus with trivial geometric inertia. All assertions apply componentwise to a finite disjoint union. Here a normal crossings divisor is a reduced effective Cartier divisor [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal] which etale locally at every point is cut out by a product of distinct members of a regular system of parameters; its global irreducible components may self-intersect, and a strict normal crossings divisor [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary] is the special case with regular components.
